ei.subject: 영어1 미래엔(김성연)
ei.title: Can AI Think, Communicate, and See the World Like Us?

fullPassage:
The history of artificial intelligence is a story of humanity's long pursuit of creating machines that can think and act like humans. In 1942, Isaac Asimov introduced his Three Laws of Robotics, which provided an early ethical framework for AI. Then in 1950, Alan Turing, often called the father of computer science, posed the question, \u201CCan machines think?\u201D He proposed the Turing test, also known as the imitation game, which determines whether a machine can exhibit intelligent behavior. If a human judge cannot distinguish a computer from a human during the test, the computer is considered to have passed.

One of the earliest attempts to make a computer communicate like a human was ELIZA, a chatbot developed between 1964 and 1967 by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT. ELIZA was designed to play the role of a psychotherapist, using simple pattern-matching techniques to respond to users. Surprisingly, many users genuinely shared their worries with ELIZA as if it were a real therapist. Although ELIZA's technology was basic, it demonstrated the potential for machines to engage in human-like conversation.

After a period known as the AI winter from 1974 to 1980, when funding and interest declined, AI research experienced a revival. In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue defeated world chess champion Garry Kasparov, demonstrating that machines could outperform humans in complex strategic tasks. By 2002, the first home robot was introduced, bringing AI into everyday life.

A significant advancement came in 2011 when Jeff Dean and Andrew Ng used a neural network with 16,000 processors to analyze 10 million random images from the internet. Without any human intervention or labels, the system taught itself to detect faces, bodies, and cats after just three days of unsupervised learning. This was a major breakthrough in demonstrating the power of neural networks.

As AI continues to evolve, it impacts all aspects of our lives. While there are concerns about job displacement and loss of control, many experts believe AI can be harnessed for the betterment of society. The key lies in developing AI responsibly and ensuring it serves humanity's best interests.

Search engines learn from our clicks, not from the accuracy of the information. For example, if a video of a cat playing a piano gets more clicks than a video of a professional piano tuner, the search engine may rank the cat video higher. This means that irrelevant information can appear relevant if it is clicked on enough times. Such mechanisms can mislead users and contribute to the spread of misinformation.

questions.passage: In 1942, Isaac Asimov introduced his Three Laws of Robotics, __________ provided an early ethical framework for AI. Then in 1950, Alan Turing, often called the father of computer science, posed the question, “Can machines think?”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 his Three Laws of Robotics(사물)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② which: 사물 선행사(Three Laws) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 불가
❌ ③ who: 사람 선행사용
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 하나, provided의 주어 필요
det.tip: 선행사(사물) + which + 동사: 사물을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: One of the earliest attempts to make a computer communicate like a human was ELIZA, a chatbot developed between 1964 and 1967 by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT. ELIZA was __________ to play the role of a psychotherapist, using simple pattern-matching techniques to respond to users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ELIZA는 심리 치료사 역할을 하도록 설계되었다(was designed). 수동태 "be + p.p." 구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ designed: was designed → 수동태 "설계되었다"
❌ ① designing: 능동 → ELIZA가 설계하는 주체가 아님
❌ ② design: 원형 → was 뒤에 원형 불가
❌ ④ to design: to부정사 → be + to부정사는 예정/의무이며 문맥 부적절
det.tip: be designed to + 동사원형: ~하도록 설계되다 (수동태)

questions.passage: He proposed the Turing test, also known as the imitation game, which determines __________ a machine can exhibit intelligent behavior. If a human judge cannot distinguish a computer from a human during the test, the computer is considered to have passed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "기계가 지능적 행동을 보일 수 있는지 여부를(whether) 판단한다"는 의미. determines의 목적절로 whether가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① whether: ~인지 아닌지(여부) → determines whether S + V
❌ ② that: 단순 사실 → "여부"의 의미 표현 불가
❌ ③ what: "무엇을" → 문맥상 여부가 적절
❌ ④ how: "어떻게" → 문맥 불일치
det.tip: determine/decide + whether: ~인지 아닌지를 판단하다/결정하다

questions.passage: In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue defeated world chess champion Garry Kasparov, __________ that machines could outperform humans in complex strategic tasks. By 2002, the first home robot was introduced, bringing AI into everyday life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(defeated)의 결과/부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문으로 현재분사 demonstrating이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② demonstrating: 결과를 나타내는 분사구문 (현재분사)
❌ ① demonstrate: 원형 → 문법적으로 불가
❌ ③ demonstrated: 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ④ to demonstrate: to부정사 → 결과 표현에 부적절
❌ ⑤ having demonstrated: 완료 분사구문 → 주절보다 앞선 동작이 아님
det.tip: 결과 분사구문: 주절, ~ing ... → "그 결과 ~하다"

questions.passage: Without any human ①<u>intervention</u> or labels, the system ②<u>taught</u> itself to detect faces, bodies, and cats after just three days of unsupervised learning. This was a major breakthrough in ③<u>demonstated</u> the power of neural networks. As AI continues to ④<u>evolve</u>, it impacts all aspects of our lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ demonstated → demonstrating: 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사(~ing)가 와야 한다. "in demonstrating the power" = 힘을 보여주는 데 있어서
det.analysis:
❌ ③ demonstated → demonstrating: in + ~ing (전치사 + 동명사)
✅ ① intervention: 명사 → 올바름
✅ ② taught: teach의 과거형 → 올바름
✅ ④ evolve: to + 동사원형 → 올바름
det.tip: 전치사(in/on/at/of) + 동명사(~ing): 전치사 뒤에는 명사/동명사가 온다

questions.passage: The history of artificial intelligence is a story of humanity's long pursuit of creating machines that can think and act like humans. In 1942, Isaac Asimov introduced his Three Laws of Robotics, which provided an early ethical framework for AI. Then in 1950, Alan Turing, often called the father of computer science, posed the question, \u201CCan machines think?\u201D He proposed the Turing test, also known as the imitation game, which determines whether a machine can exhibit intelligent behavior. If a human judge cannot distinguish a computer from a human during the test, the computer is considered to have passed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "Alan Turing, often called the father of computer science, posed the question, 'Can machines think?'" → Turing이 "기계가 생각할 수 있는가?" 질문을 제기했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Turing이 "Can machines think?" 질문 제기: 본문과 일치
❌ ① 컴퓨터 과학의 아버지는 Asimov가 아닌 Turing
❌ ③ 튜링 테스트는 1950년에 제안
❌ ④ ELIZA는 Joseph Weizenbaum이 개발
det.tip: 인물과 업적을 정확히 매칭: Asimov = 로봇 3법칙, Turing = 튜링 테스트

ch: Isaac Asimov는 컴퓨터 과학의 아버지라 불린다.
Alan Turing은 "기계가 생각할 수 있는가?"라는 질문을 제기했다.

questions.passage: One of the earliest attempts to make a computer communicate like a human was ELIZA, a chatbot developed between 1964 and 1967 by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT. ELIZA was designed to play the role of a psychotherapist, using simple pattern-matching techniques to respond to users. Surprisingly, many users genuinely shared their worries with ELIZA as if it were a real therapist. Although ELIZA's technology was basic, it demonstrated the potential for machines to engage in human-like conversation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "many users genuinely shared their worries with ELIZA as if it were a real therapist" → 사용자들은 마치 진짜 치료사인 것처럼 걱정을 나눴다. 따라서 "즉시 알아챘다"는 불일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 사용자들은 기계임을 즉시 알아챘다: 본문과 반대 → "as if it were a real therapist"
✅ ① MIT에서 개발: "by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT" 일치
✅ ② 패턴 매칭: "pattern-matching techniques" 일치
✅ ④ 심리 치료사 역할: "play the role of a psychotherapist" 일치
det.tip: "as if + 가정법": 마치 ~인 것처럼 → 실제로는 아님을 암시

ch: ELIZA의 사용자들은 그것이 기계임을 즉시 알아챘다.
ELIZA는 심리 치료사 역할을 하도록 설계되었다.

questions.passage: The history of artificial intelligence is a story of humanity's long pursuit of creating machines that can think and act like humans. In 1942, Isaac Asimov introduced his Three Laws of Robotics, which provided an early ethical framework for AI. Then in 1950, Alan Turing, often called the father of computer science, posed the question, \u201CCan machines think?\u201D He proposed the Turing test, also known as the imitation game, which determines whether a machine can exhibit intelligent behavior. If a human judge cannot distinguish a computer from a human during the test, the computer is considered to have passed.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "The history of artificial intelligence is a story of humanity's long pursuit" + 1942년부터 현재까지의 주요 사건들 → AI의 발전 역사와 주요 이정표
det.analysis:
✅ ③ AI의 발전 역사와 주요 이정표: 첫 문장 "The history of AI" + 연도별 사건 나열
❌ ① 일자리 대체 경고: 본문의 부분적 언급, 주제 아님
❌ ② 신경망 작동 원리: 한 단락의 소재일 뿐
❌ ④ 윤리 규범 법적 효력: 언급 없음
det.tip: 글의 주제: 첫 문장 "The history of artificial intelligence"가 핵심 단서

ch: AI가 인간의 일자리를 완전히 대체할 것이라는 경고
신경망의 기술적 작동 원리에 대한 상세한 설명

questions.passage: He proposed the Turing test, also known as the __________, which determines whether a machine can exhibit intelligent behavior. If a human judge cannot distinguish a computer from a human during the test, the computer is considered to have passed. Turing predicted that machines would eventually be considered intelligent.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 튜링 테스트는 모방 게임(imitation game)으로도 알려져 있다. 기계가 인간을 모방하여 구분할 수 없으면 통과.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ imitation game: "also known as the imitation game" → 원문 표현
❌ ① ethical framework: 윤리적 틀 → 아시모프의 로봇 법칙과 관련
❌ ② pattern-matching: ELIZA의 기술
❌ ④ neural network: 2011년 실험과 관련
det.tip: Turing test = imitation game: 기계가 인간처럼 행동할 수 있는지 판별

questions.passage: A significant advancement came in 2011 when Jeff Dean and Andrew Ng used a neural network with 16,000 processors to analyze 10 million random images from the internet. Without any human intervention or labels, the system taught itself to detect faces, bodies, and cats after just three days of __________ learning.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "Without any human intervention or labels" → 인간의 개입이나 라벨 없이 스스로 학습 = 비지도 학습(unsupervised learning)
det.analysis:
✅ ① unsupervised: 인간 개입 없이 스스로 학습 → 비지도 학습
❌ ② supervised: 라벨 있는 지도 학습 → "without labels"와 모순
❌ ③ reinforced: 보상 기반 강화 학습 → 문맥과 불일치
❌ ④ manual: 수동 → "taught itself"와 모순
det.tip: unsupervised learning: 라벨/지도 없이 데이터에서 패턴을 스스로 찾는 학습

questions.passage: Search engines learn from our clicks, not from the accuracy of the information. This means that irrelevant information can appear relevant if it is clicked on enough times. Such mechanisms can mislead users and contribute to the spread of __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 무관한 정보가 관련 있어 보이고, 사용자를 오도하는 메커니즘 → 잘못된 정보(misinformation)의 확산에 기여
det.analysis:
✅ ① misinformation(잘못된 정보): mislead + irrelevant info → 허위정보 확산
❌ ② innovation(혁신): 부정적 맥락과 불일치
❌ ③ optimization(최적화): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ personalization(개인화): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: mislead(오도하다) + irrelevant information → misinformation(잘못된 정보) 확산

questions.passage: The history of __________ (artifice) intelligence is a story of humanity's long pursuit of creating machines that can think and act like humans. In 1942, Isaac Asimov introduced his Three Laws of Robotics.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: artifice(명사, 기교) → artificial(형용사): 명사 intelligence를 수식하는 형용사 필요. "인공적인 지능"
det.analysis:
artifice(명사) → artificial(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 intelligence(명사)를 수식하는 형용사가 필요
artificial intelligence = 인공 지능
det.tip: artifice → artificial / benefit → beneficial / office → official — 명사 → -ial 형용사 변환

questions.passage: A __________ (significance) advancement came in 2011 when Jeff Dean and Andrew Ng used a neural network with 16,000 processors to analyze 10 million random images from the internet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: significance(명사) → significant(형용사): 명사 advancement를 수식하는 형용사 필요. "중대한 발전"
det.analysis:
significance(명사) → significant(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 advancement(명사)를 수식하는 형용사가 필요
significant advancement = 중대한 발전
det.tip: significance → significant / importance → important / difference → different — 명사 → 형용사 변환

questions.passage: One of the earliest attempts to make a computer communicate like a human was ELIZA, a chatbot developed between 1964 and 1967 by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT. questions.stem: 다음 글에서 ELIZA가 수행하도록 설계된 역할을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "ELIZA was designed to play the role of a psychotherapist" → 심리 치료사
det.analysis:
ELIZA의 역할 = a psychotherapist
1단어 답 = psychotherapist
det.tip: "play the role of ~" = ~의 역할을 하다 → 역할을 찾는 문제

questions.passage: As AI continues to evolve, it impacts all aspects of our lives. While there are concerns about job displacement and loss of control, many experts believe AI can be harnessed for the betterment of society. The key lies in developing AI responsibly and ensuring it serves humanity's best interests.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 많은 전문가들이 AI가 기여할 수 있다고 믿는 것을 "the __________ of society" 형태로 본문에서 1단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "AI can be harnessed for the betterment of society" → 사회의 개선/향상
det.analysis:
많은 전문가 = many experts believe
AI의 목적 = the betterment of society = 사회의 향상
det.tip: betterment = 개선, 향상 — better(더 나은) + -ment(명사 접미사)

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 튜링 테스트에서 인간 심판이 할 수 없어야 통과가 되는 행위를 나타내는 동사 1단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "If a human judge cannot distinguish a computer from a human" → 컴퓨터와 인간을 구별하다
det.analysis:
튜링 테스트 통과 조건 = 인간 심판이 구별할 수 없을 때
동사 = distinguish (구별하다)
det.tip: distinguish A from B = A와 B를 구별하다 — 튜링 테스트의 핵심 개념

det.korean: "In 1942, Isaac Asimov introduced his Three Laws of Robotics" → 1942년에 아시모프가 로봇 3법칙을 소개했다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 "In 1942, Isaac Asimov introduced his Three Laws of Robotics"와 정확히 일치

questions.stem:

questions.passage: Search engines learn from our clicks, not from the accuracy of the information. For example, if a video of a cat playing a piano gets more clicks than a video of a professional piano tuner, the search engine may rank the cat video higher. This means that irrelevant information can appear relevant if it is clicked on enough times. Such mechanisms can mislead users and contribute to the spread of misinformation.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Search engines rank information based on accuracy rather than the number of clicks."

det.korean: 본문: "Search engines learn from our clicks, not from the accuracy of the information" → 검색 엔진은 정확성이 아닌 클릭 수에서 학습한다. 따라서 "정확성에 기반"은 False.
det.analysis:
❌ False: 본문 "learn from clicks, not from accuracy" → 클릭 기반(✓), 정확성 기반(✗)
진술은 정반대
det.tip: 인과 관계를 정확히 파악: 순위 결정 요인 = 클릭 수(✓) ≠ 정확성(✗)
